title: Custom useControlled State Hook (Radix / MUI Pattern)
problemStatement: Implement `useControlledState({ controlled, default: defaultVal })` that mimics the standard pattern used in Radix UI and Material UI, returning `[currentValue, setValue]`.
interviewTrap: Components often need to be either controlled by a parent or self-contained. The useControlled pattern allows reusable UI widgets (accordion, modal, combobox) to support both flawlessly.

testCases.name: Uncontrolled mode updates internal value
testCases.testFn: const [val, setVal] = useControlledState({ default: 'closed' }); return setVal('opened');

testCases.name: Controlled mode reflects external prop value
testCases.testFn: const [val] = useControlledState({ controlled: 'fixed', default: 'ignored' }); return val;

testCases.name: Supports functional updater syntax
testCases.testFn: const [val, setVal] = useControlledState({ default: 5 }); return setVal(prev => prev + 1);

details.name: Controlled mode reflects external prop value

detailedExplanation.conceptualOverview: A controlled component's single source of truth is React state; an uncontrolled component delegates state to the DOM node via a ref. Bridging both requires synchronizing internal fallback state with incoming prop state.
stepByStepWalkthrough: 1. Render Phase: Fiber node evaluation and hooks linked-list dispatch for Derived State & Controlled Prop Inversion.
2. Reconciliation: Double buffering and fiber diffing mechanics.
3. Commit Phase: Synchronous/passive effect execution and DOM mutation.
detailedExplanation.underlyingEngineInternals: In React Fiber, Derived State & Controlled Prop Inversion maintains state across work-in-progress trees and lanes scheduling priority.

interviewCrossQuestions.question: How does Radix UI and MUI's useControlled hook work?
interviewCrossQuestions.answer: `useControlled({ controlled, default, name })` manages state that can be either controlled by the caller or uncontrolled internally. It creates an internal `useState(default)`. If `controlled !== undefined`, it returns `[controlled, setControlled]`; if `controlled === undefined`, it returns `[internalState, setInternalState]`. It warns in development if a component switches between the two modes.
interviewCrossQuestions.whyAsked: Core design system state abstraction question.

realWorldUseCases.description: Radix primitives supporting both controlled (`open` + `onOpenChange`) and uncontrolled (`defaultOpen`) modes.
realWorldUseCases.codeSnippet: const [isOpen, setIsOpen] = useControllableState({ prop: open, defaultProp: defaultOpen, onChange: onOpenChange });

howToExplain.opening: useControlled allows UI primitives to seamlessly support both controlled and uncontrolled usage without duplicating state logic.
keyPoints: Inspects whether the controlled prop is defined.
Falls back to internal state if controlled prop is omitted.
Dispatches external onChange callbacks in both modes.
Standard architecture for headless UI libraries (Radix, MUI).
howToExplain.closingImpression: useControlled gives component consumers the flexibility to choose between simple drop-in usage and tight external control.
analogies: A car with dual-mode transmission: you can drive in automatic mode (uncontrolled internal state) or switch to paddle shifters (controlled external state).

commonMistakes.mistake: Syncing controlled props to internal state using useEffect.
commonMistakes.why: Creates an unnecessary extra render pass and causes visual desynchronization.
commonMistakes.correct: Derive state directly during render: `const value = prop !== undefined ? prop : internalState`.

followUpDeepDive.question: Why does the React team discourage deriving state from props (getDerivedStateFromProps)?
followUpDeepDive.answer: Duplicating props into state creates two sources of truth that frequently become desynchronized. React recommends either fully controlled components or fully uncontrolled components with a key.
followUpDeepDive.specReference: React Blog: You Probably Don't Need Derived State
